cards.front: Recall a key point about Building Your Portfolio Component 1
cards.back: Component 1 (Portfolio) is worth 60% — it must show a sustained project plus supporting studies that demonstrate all four AOs.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Building Your Portfolio Component 1
cards.back: Your portfolio should show a CLEAR NARRATIVE: from starting point, through research and experimentation, to a resolved personal response.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Building Your Portfolio Component 1
cards.back: Supporting studies show breadth — additional experiments, artist responses and explorations that complement your main project.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Building Your Portfolio Component 1
cards.back: Written annotation must use specialist vocabulary and show REFLECTIVE THINKING — not just descriptions of what you did.

cards.front: What should you know about art, craft and design exam tips?
cards.back: MAP your portfolio against the four AOs — can a moderator see evidence of each? Include PROCESS work (thumbnails, experiments, test pieces) alongside final outcomes. Annotate REFLECTIVELY throughout. Show SUPPORTING STUDIES for breadth. Organise with clear narrative flow.

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: A portfolio is just a collection of your best finished pieces of artwork. Correct: A portfolio is EVIDENCE OF YOUR CREATIVE JOURNEY, not a gallery of finished pieces. AQA assesses how you DEVELOPED ideas (AO1), EXPERIMENTED (AO2), RECORDED (AO3) and PRESENTED (AO4).
